# Brightfield Ingest API

The Ingest API lets you push event data directly into a Brightfield Analytics workspace without
going through the batch upload UI. It's the recommended path for anything higher than ~10k
events/day.

> **Note:** This replaces the old `/v1/events` endpoint, which is deprecated and will be removed
> on 2026-09-01. See [Migration](#migration-from-v1) below.

## Authentication

All requests require a workspace API key passed as a bearer token.

```
Authorization: Bearer bf_live_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
```

Keys are scoped to a single workspace and can be rotated from **Settings â†’ API Keys**. Test-mode
keys (prefixed `bf_test_`) write to a sandbox dataset that's cleared every 24h.

## Endpoints

### POST /v2/events

Send a single event or a batch of up to 500 events.

**Request body**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `event_name` | string | yes | Name of the event, e.g. `purchase_completed` |
| `timestamp` | string (ISO 8601) | no | Defaults to receipt time if omitted |
| `user_id` | string | yes | Stable identifier for the actor |
| `properties` | object | no | Arbitrary key/value event metadata |

Example:

```json
{
  "event_name": "purchase_completed",
  "timestamp": "2026-02-10T18:32:04Z",
  "user_id": "usr_8f2a1",
  "properties": {
    "amount": 42.50,
    "currency": "USD",
    "items": 3
  }
}
```

Response: `202 Accepted` with an empty body on success. Events are processed asynchronously; use
the [Query API](#query-api-reference-elsewhere) to confirm ingestion (usually within 30s).

### GET /v2/events/schema

Returns the currently inferred schema for your workspace's event stream. Useful for debugging
type mismatches.

no request body needed for this one, just hit it with your API key.

### DELETE /v2/events/{event_id}

Deletes a single event by ID. Only available on Enterprise plans. Deletions are eventually
consistent and can take up to 15 minutes to propagate to downstream dashboards.

## Rate limits

| Plan | Requests/sec | Burst |
|---|---|---|
| Starter | 10 | 20 |
| Growth | 50 | 100 |
| Enterprise | 500 | 1000 |

Exceeding your rate limit returns `429 Too Many Requests` with a `Retry-After` header. We
recommend client-side batching (up to 500 events per call) rather than firing individual requests.

## Error codes

- `400` â€” malformed JSON or missing required field
- `401` â€” invalid or expired API key
- `413` â€” batch exceeds 500 events or 1MB payload
- `422` â€” event_name doesn't match your workspace's naming policy (if enforced)
- `429` â€” rate limit exceeded
- `5xx` â€” internal error, safe to retry with exponential backoff

## SDKs

Official SDKs exist for:
- **Node.js** â€” `npm install @brightfield/ingest`
- **Python** â€” `pip install brightfield-ingest`
- Go, Ruby, and Java are community-maintained and not officially supported. Use at your own risk!

## Migration from v1

The old `/v1/events` endpoint used a flat structure with `props` instead of `properties`, and did
not support batching. There's no automated migration tool â€” you'll need to update your
integration code manually. Reach out in #ingest-api-support if you get stuck.

### Field mapping

| v1 field | v2 field | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `props` | `properties` | Same shape, renamed |
| `uid` | `user_id` | Renamed for clarity |
| `ts` | `timestamp` | Now requires ISO 8601, v1 accepted unix epoch |
| N/A | (batching) | v2 only â€” send up to 500 events per request |

---

*Questions? Post in #ingest-api-support or email platform-team@brightfieldanalytics.example.

NimbusDB Administration Guide
Version 4.2  |  Last updated: March 2025  |  Internal Engineering Documentation
1. Overview
NimbusDB is a distributed, column-oriented database designed for high-throughput analytical
workloads. This guide covers installation, cluster configuration, backup procedures, and
troubleshooting for administrators responsible for production deployments. It assumes familiarity with
Linux system administration and basic networking concepts.
1.1 Supported Platforms
NimbusDB officially supports Ubuntu 20.04+, RHEL 8+, and Debian 11+. Docker and Kubernetes
deployments are supported via the official Helm chart. macOS is supported for local development only
and is NOT recommended for production use.
2. Installation
Download the release tarball matching your platform from the internal artifact repository. The following
commands install NimbusDB on a standard Ubuntu host:
 curl -O https://artifacts.internal/nimbusdb/nimbusdb-4.2.0-linux-amd64.tar.gz
tar -xzf nimbusdb-4.2.0-linux-amd64.tar.gz
sudo ./install.sh --data-dir /var/lib/nimbusdb --config /etc/nimbusdb/nimbus.conf
Note: The installer requires root privileges to create the nimbusdb system user and register the systemd
service. If you are installing in a container, use --no-systemd to skip this step.
2.1 Minimum Hardware Requirements

3. Cluster Configuration
A NimbusDB cluster consists of one or more coordinator nodes and a pool of worker nodes.
Coordinators handle query planning and metadata; workers store and process data shards. For fault
tolerance, run an odd number of coordinators (3 or 5) to maintain quorum.
3.1 Key Configuration Parameters

cluster.replication_factor — number of copies of each shard (default: 3)


cluster.quorum_reads — require majority acknowledgment on reads (default: false)

storage.compaction_interval — background compaction frequency (default: 6h)

network.heartbeat_timeout_ms — node failure detection threshold (default: 5000)

4. Backup and Recovery
Nightly snapshots are taken automatically when backup.enabled is set to true. Snapshots are written to
the configured object store target and retained according to backup.retention_days. Point-in-time
recovery is supported for up to 30 days by replaying the write-ahead log against the nearest snapshot.
WARNING: Restoring a snapshot to a running cluster will overwrite existing data on the target shards.
Always restore to a scratch cluster first and verify data integrity before promoting.
4.1 Manual Backup Procedure
1
Put the target coordinator into maintenance mode: nimbusctl maintenance enable
2
Trigger a manual snapshot: nimbusctl backup create --label pre-migration
3
Verify the snapshot manifest was written to the object store
4
Disable maintenance mode: nimbusctl maintenance disable
5. Troubleshooting
Common issues and resolutions are summarized below.
Symptom
Likely Cause
Resolution
Node marked DOWN repeatedly
Network latency spikes
Increase heartbeat_timeout_ms
Slow query planning
Stale statistics
Run nimbusctl analyze <table>
Disk usage growing unbounded
Compaction disabled/failing
Check compaction logs, re-enable
For further assistance, contact the Database Reliability team on #nimbusdb-support.

Remote Work & Expense Policy
Doc ID: POL-HR-014      Effective: Jan 1, 2024      Rev. 3 (unreviewed since Aug 2024)
1. Purpose
This policy explains what the company will and will not reimburse for employees working remotely,
and clarifies expectations around availability, equipment, and travel. It replaces the interim WFH
guidance circulated during 2021 and applies to all full-time staff.
2. WHO THIS APPLIES TO
All full-time employees classified as remote or hybrid. Contractors should refer to their individual
agreements — this policy does NOT apply to contractors, interns, or seasonal staff unless
explicitly stated otherwise in their offer letter.
3. Home office stipend
Employees receive a one-time $500 stipend for home office setup, and an ongoing $40/month toward
internet costs. The one-time stipend must be claimed within 90 days of start date or it expires. no
extensions will be granted except in cases approved by a VP.

4. TRAVEL FOR IN-PERSON MEETINGS
Remote employees required to travel to a company office or offsite are reimbursed for coach-class
flights, standard hotel rooms (up to $220/night in major metros, $160/night elsewhere), and ground
transportation. Receipts are required for anything over $25. Submit expenses via the Expense
Portal within 14 days of travel — late submissions may be denied at manager discretion.
5. equipment & IT
IT-issued laptops remain company property and must be returned upon termination. Employees
needing a second monitor, docking station, or ergonomic accessories should file a request through

the IT Helpdesk; approval typically takes 2-3 business days.
6. QUESTIONS
Direct questions about this policy to peopleops@company.example or post in #ask-people-ops.

Brightfield Analytics delivered revenue of $48.2M in Q3 2025, up 14% year-over-year, driven primarily
by growth in our enterprise data-platform segment. Gross margin held steady at 71%. We closed the
quarter with $112M in cash and equivalents and no outstanding debt. Customer count grew to 1,840, a
net addition of 96 accounts during the quarter.
